subject: Technical workshop: SDK streaming + tool/function-calling — scheduling
messages:
From: Alex Thornton <alex@healsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: technical workshop on SDK streaming + tool calls

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our engineering and product teams at HealSync would like a focused technical workshop that covers: SDK usage for low-latency streaming, best practices for function/tool calling (especially around safety and structured outputs), and integration patterns for KV/prefix caching.

Attendees: Alex Thornton (eng lead), Priya Rao (product), procurement@healsync.com (ops).

Can your team run a 60–90 minute session next week? Prefer afternoons PST. Also looking for a short agenda and any pre-reads or sample code we should review.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Alex Thornton
Head of Engineering, HealSync
alex@healsync.com
[Attachment: healsync-integration-outline.docx (DOCX)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thornton <alex@healsync.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: technical workshop on SDK streaming + tool calls

Hi Alex —

Thanks, this is great. We can absolutely run a focused session. Two quick questions: do you want an emphasis on a hosted API workflow (no infra changes) or a hybrid/dedicated setup? Also, do you want us to include a short demo of function calling safety patterns (structured JSON + validation)?

Proposed slots (PST):
- Tue Nov 2, 2:00–3:30pm
- Wed Nov 3, 3:00–4:30pm

Proposed short agenda (attached):
1) 10m — goals and current architecture from HealSync
2) 25m — SDK streaming demo (continuous output, reconnects, partial responses)
3) 20m — function/tool calling patterns + validation and fallback
4) 15m — caching/batching recommendations and cost notes
5) 10m — Q&A and next steps

I attached a draft agenda and a small sample repo we can walkthrough. Karthik and Ava will join for the demo and kernel/latency discussion. If those slots don’t work, tell me 2 alternatives and we’ll adapt.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: Redwood_Workshop_Agenda_v2.pdf (PDF)]

+1 on the Nov 2nd slot — works for engineering.

Quick note on content: we'll include a short live run of the Node and Python SDK streaming patterns, a sample of function-calling with schema validation via our JSON schema helper, and a short segment on quantization/latency tradeoffs for small batches. Priyom will bring the integration checklist to walk through typical token-cost mitigations.

Also sharing a tiny artifact: redwood-sdk-streaming-sample.zip (see attachment) — it contains the sample client and prompts we plan to run.

—Karthik
